extracted.intended_audience: Detroit residents, local community members, and civic-minded readers
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial priorities and framing used on a local-news homepage for Outlier Media focused on Detroit: what stories to publish, what purposes coverage should serve, and how to engage the community. This covers mission statements, topical tags, investigative selection priorities, service journalism, and community-engagement programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local
rubrics_metrics.description: Local — coverage focused on Detroit and issues that matter to Detroiters (implicit in the tagline 'Local, accountable, informed' and the site's content selection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories and resources should be directly relevant to Detroit residents (neighborhood events, city budgets, local government actions, housing issues). Examples on the page: housing/foreclosure stories, Detroit budget hearings, local events guides. Emphasize geographic relevance and tangible impact on daily life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountable — journalism that holds power to account (part of the tagline 'Local, accountable, informed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that scrutinizes government, agencies, corporations, and other institutions affecting Detroiters. Examples: investigation into Wayne County foreclosures, coverage of police cooperation with federal immigration agents, stories about Detroit job training agency deficits. Use public records, watchdog reporting, and highlight lack of transparency or failures in process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Informed — provide residents with clear, useful information (part of the tagline 'Local, accountable, informed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce reporting and guides that educate readers about what is happening and how it affects them. Examples: FOIA 101, Open Meetings Act guide, resource lists for shelters and assistance programs. Emphasize clarity, actionable steps, and factual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service journalism / 'At your service'
rubrics_metrics.description: At your service — 'We identify, report and deliver valuable information that helps residents create more accountability around issues they care about.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should be oriented toward helping residents take action or get relief: identifying problems, explaining remedies, and delivering practical next steps. Examples: 'How to preapply for home repair help', guides to claiming auction profits, and instructions for obtaining public records. Tone should be pragmatic and oriented to public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability Spotlight / Investigations selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountability Spotlight: series and investigations that 'shine a light on issues where better information alone can’t make a difference and where a lack of accountability causes harm to Detroiters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select investigative projects where documenting facts and exposing wrongdoing or opacity can lead to real-world accountability or change. These stories should be deep, series-style where necessary, and target harms caused by institutional failures (e.g., opaque foreclosure processes, misuse of public funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix This First (actionable/problem-solving focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix This First — a thematic priority that highlights immediate problems that demand repair or policy attention (tag used extensively across the homepage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that identifies urgent, solvable problems and explains what should be done, who’s responsible, and how residents are affected. Examples: pieces about home-repair funding shortfalls, predatory tax-assistance companies, and immediate threats to housing stability. Provide concrete steps and expose barriers to fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems Repair (focus on systemic failures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems Repair — coverage centered on persistent, system-level breakdowns (housing, courts, public benefits, policing, immigration services) and their effects on residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how institutional arrangements, budgets, staffing, procedures, and policies create harm or leave needs unmet. Examples: stories about an underfunded immigrants office, Detroit's home-repair funding gap, county auction/profit issues. Emphasize root causes and systemic remedies, not just individual anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement and Documenters program
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenters / Community — actively engage residents in reporting (train and pay community members to cover public meetings and civic processes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit, train, and compensate community members to attend and report on local meetings. Encourage participation through orientations and featured profiles (e.g., 'Meet Nick Kramer' and 'Meet Paul Enns'). Use community-contributed reporting to expand coverage and make government more transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical guides and how-to content
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides / How-to — produce practical, how-to resources that help residents navigate civic processes and access services (e.g., 'FOIA 101', Open Meetings Act guide, lists of shelters and assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear, step-by-step explainers and resource lists that enable readers to take action (file FOIA requests, apply for repair programs, find shelters). Make materials accessible, linked, and up-to-date; emphasize eligibility, deadlines, and contact information where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free and accessible information / newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Make important information widely available and free (e.g., 'Sign up for our newsletter... Straight to your inbox and always free').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting and resources are freely accessible to the public; use newsletters and outreach to distribute time-sensitive information (deadlines, events, urgent alerts). Aim for concise, actionable summaries for busy readers.
